key_insight: In epitaxial CsPbBr3 single crystals, terahertz and Hall mobilities match quantitatively, indicating truly intrinsic charge transport across macroscopic length scales.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical benchmark and measurement strategy for verifying defect-free mobility in soft-lattice perovskites and other emerging semiconductors.
method: Concurrent optical pump-terahertz probe and Hall-effect measurements on the same single-crystal sample
Dedicated device platform for comparing local ultrafast mobility with macroscopic transport mobility
Temperature-dependent mobility analysis to test band-like transport behavior
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent room-temperature hole mobilities of about 30 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 and similar temperature-power exponents from both OPTP and Hall measurements.
watch_item: The conclusion is demonstrated on epitaxial CsPbBr3 single crystals, so extending the same intrinsic-transport claim to more defective polycrystalline films or other perovskite compositions may require additional validation.
paper_title: Matching Terahertz and Hall Mobilities as a Hallmark of Intrinsic Charge Transport in Metal-Halide Perovskites
